course_name_original: Termodinámica aplicada y transmisión de calor

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of applied thermodynamics and heat transfer. Basic principles and their application to solving engineering problems.

syllabus_topics: Introduction and basic concepts. The scope of thermodynamics. Dimensions and units. General definitions. Other basic definitions.
Principles of Thermodynamics. Zeroth Principle. First Principle in closed and open systems. Second Principle in closed and open systems.
Introduction. Phase diagrams. Equations of state. Calculation of thermodynamic properties.
Combustion. Introduction. Combustion reactions. Calculation of enthalpies of formation and combustion. Energy balances in combustion processes.
Gas power cycles. Introduction to heat engines. Carnot cycle. Standard air assumptions. Otto cycle. Diesel cycle. Brayton cycle. Brayton cycle modifications.
Vapor power cycles. Rankine cycle. Rankine cycle modifications to increase efficiency. Combined cycles. Cogeneration. Binary cycles. Equipment.
Refrigeration cycles. Inverted Carnot cycle. Vapor compression refrigeration cycle. Gas refrigeration cycles. Absorption refrigeration systems. Heat pump.
Psychrometry. Humidity. Enthalpy of moist air. Moist air mixtures. Psychrometric chart.
Introduction to heat transfer. Generalities. Heat transfer mechanisms. Applications.

assessment_methods.method: Seminars on Practical and/or Theoretical Case Resolution

assessment_rules: The general evaluation model is continuous assessment. Seminars (5%) are not re-evaluable, with each seminar representing 2.5% of the total grade. Laboratory practices (20%) require mandatory attendance and a minimum grade of 4, and are re-evaluable. Two written tests (37.5% each) cover topics 1-5 and 6-9, respectively; in each test, both the theory and problems sections require a minimum of 4.0, and the overall exam requires a minimum of 4.5 to be averaged. Students who do not pass the ordinary call or did not attend may take the extraordinary call only for the re-evaluable activities not passed. Written tests penalize 0.25 points per spelling mistake and up to 20% for disorder or illegibility.
